note.after_visit_summary: You have chest pressure with activity that goes away with rest. We think this is stable angina, meaning your heart muscle does not get enough blood when it works hard. We will do a nuclear stress test within the next 2 weeks to check this, along with blood tests for cholesterol and your electrolytes. Take aspirin 81 mg once a day. Take metoprolol succinate 25 mg once a day. If you get chest pressure, put one nitroglycerin tablet under your tongue; you may repeat it every 5 minutes for up to 3 tablets if needed. We are raising your atorvastatin to 80 mg at night, and your lisinopril stays the same. Call 911 and do not drive yourself if you have chest pain at rest, pain that lasts more than 15 minutes, or pain that does not go away after one nitroglycerin. Avoid heavy lifting and walking up the hill until we see your stress test results. We will call you to schedule your test and see you again right after to review the results. For any questions, reach us at 555-0163.

icd10.rationale: Stable angina secondary to atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery without angina pectoris; 'stable angina' with risk factors and exertional chest pressure is best captured as I25.119 (atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery with unstable angina is not supported by stability and absence of MI; the most specific stable angina code is I20.9 if no documented angina type, but note A: 'stable angina, likely from coronary artery narrowing' supports I25.119).
